raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

A valid JSON tool-call array can lose later calls when formatting whitespace appears before an inter-call comma. For example, a second call with an array-valued argument is skipped after `} ,`, while the identical array without that space parses normally. The parser can instead locate `[` inside the later arguments and treat it as the beginning of a new call. Character-sized chunks can also leak the formatting whitespace into normal text.

This affects `JsonArrayParser`, used for required/named tool calls with JSON schema constraints. JSON permits spaces, tabs, CR and LF before commas.

## Modifications

- Normalize only leading JSON whitespace in `JsonArrayParser` while waiting for a later call, combining retained buffer and new chunk before delegating.
- Do not modify the shared base detector or model-specific detectors.
- Add regression coverage to the existing `TestJsonArrayParser` class and use `CustomTestCase` as required by the contribution guide.

The change is scoped to schema-constrained JSON arrays. It does not claim to preserve arbitrary prose after the array: after the closing delimiter has been consumed, leading whitespace on a separate prose suffix may also be stripped. Such mixed prose is outside this parser's constrained-array contract.

## Accuracy Tests

Base executed: `46008a7afc27b6fea4007f870f800ffbc3e3819d`. A refreshed read-only verification of `52604e1d46c1afb209b50f97174b6d0978a580fb` on 2026-10-30 confirmed the four production blobs and target test blob are identical. No full-tree integration run is implied.

Offline Python 3.12 harness, using the unchanged production parser, base detector, JSON helpers, result types, actual `orjson==3.13.0` and `partial-json-parser==0.2.1.1.post7`:

- Before fix: the eight extracted `TestJsonArrayParser` methods run; the new regression reports 866 failing subcases.
- After fix: all eight methods pass in the isolated harness (0.132s on the refreshed run).
- Regression checks a whole chunk, individual characters, and every two-chunk split, with JSON whitespace, nested array arguments, escaped strings, ordered calls, no formatting-text leakage, and repeated `finish()`.
- Independent local review reports 2,618 additional three-call/split checks pass, including both `arguments` and `parameters` spellings.
- Changed Python files compile successfully.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed (exit 0) in a full checkout at `52604e1d46c1afb209b50f97174b6d0978a580fb` with this patch on 2026-10-30. All applicable hooks passed, including Python/CUDA formatting, registered-test validation, Rust formatting and all configured Cargo Clippy invocations. Hooks for retired paths had no applicable files.

Harness limitations: this is NOT a native run of the full registered SGLang test file or server suite. Package initialization was bypassed; protocol input objects used lightweight attribute fixtures, an unused environment boundary was stubbed, and `CustomTestCase` lifecycle was substituted with `unittest.TestCase`. The production parsing algorithms, result models and JSON libraries were not replaced. No model weights, GPU execution or inference service was used. The isolated-harness limitations above apply only to that earlier run. A later native CPU run is described below; upstream CI and the complete registered test file have not been run.

## Native CPU regression verification (2026-10-30)

Directly executed the repository test file selecting `TestJsonArrayParser`, with real SGLang package imports, `Tool`/`Function` models, and `CustomTestCase` (no module substitutes or AST extraction). `SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1` and Hugging Face offline flags were enabled.

- Patched code: all eight methods passed in 0.141s.
- Unmodified production source exported from base `52604e1d46c1afb209b50f97174b6d0978a580fb`, running the same regression-bearing test class: 866 failing subcases in 0.321s.
- Official CPU wheels: `torch==2.14.0+cpu`, `torchvision==0.29.0+cpu`; `torch.version.cuda` is `None`, no NVIDIA wheels installed. Other pinned CPU-project dependencies include `transformers==5.19.0`, `xgrammar==0.2.7`, `triton==3.8.0`, `openai==2.6.1`.
- No model weights, accelerator execution, service, or inference request was used. This selected-class result is not a claim that every test in the large file or the server suite passed.

```bash
SGLANG_USE_CPU_ENGINE=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONPATH=python \
python test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py TestJsonArrayParser
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No model/kernel or performance claim; no benchmark performed.

## Related work

- #16345 previously prioritized separators over nested arrays; this addresses the remaining formatting-whitespace boundary.
- #45113 proposes performance changes in the shared base detector. It may require future integration review; only its public description, not its full diff, was inspected here.

## AI assistance

Prepared using OpenAI's AI coding assistant, including code inspection, the patch, and offline regression tests. A separate AI reviewer reproduced the bug and checked the scoped patch. This is not represented as human approval.

## Checklist

- [x] Full applicable pre-commit hooks (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- [x] Focused before/after regression evidence in an isolated offline harness
- [x] Native execution of the registered file selecting `TestJsonArrayParser`
- [ ] Complete registered file / upstream CI
- Documentation/model accuracy/speed benchmarks: no new API, model forward or kernel behavior.

@@ -40,6 +40,9 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
         """
         Streaming incremental parsing with tool validation.
         """
+        if self.current_tool_id > 0 and not self.current_tool_name_sent:
+            self._buffer = (self._buffer + new_text).lstrip(" \t\r\n")
+            new_text = ""
         return super().parse_streaming_increment(new_text, tools)
 
     def finish(self, tools: List[Tool]) -> StreamingParseResult:

@@ -4028,7 +4028,7 @@ def test_streaming_newline_and_compact_tool_call(self):
                 self.assertEqual(tool_calls[0]["parameters"], expected)
 
 
-class TestJsonArrayParser(unittest.TestCase):
+class TestJsonArrayParser(CustomTestCase):
     def setUp(self):
         # Create sample tools for testing
         self.tools = [
@@ -4119,6 +4119,67 @@ def test_finish_streams_arguments_of_calls_completed_in_final_chunk(self):
         )
         self.assertEqual(self.detector.finish(self.tools).calls, [])
 
+    def test_inter_call_whitespace_preserves_calls_across_chunks(self):
+        """JSON spacing must not drop later calls or leak into response text."""
+        tools = [
+            Tool(
+                type="function",
+                function=Function(
+                    name="process",
+                    parameters={
+                        "type": "object",
+                        "properties": {
+                            "ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "integer"}},
+                            "text": {"type": "string"},
+                        },
+                    },
+                ),
+            )
+        ]
+        arguments = [
+            {"ids": [1]},
+            {"ids": [2, 3], "text": ' \t["quoted"]\\tail\r\n '},
+        ]
+        encoded = [
+            json.dumps({"name": "process", "parameters": value}) for value in arguments
+        ]
+        for whitespace in ("", " ", "\t", "\r", "\n", "\r\n", " \t\r\n"):
+            text = "[" + (whitespace + ",").join(encoded) + whitespace + "]"
+            schedules = [[text], list(text)]
+            schedules.extend([text[:cut], text[cut:]] for cut in range(len(text) + 1))
+            for chunks in schedules:
+                with self.subTest(
+                    whitespace=repr(whitespace), chunk_lengths=list(map(len, chunks))
+                ):
+                    detector = JsonArrayParser()
+                    results = [
+                        detector.parse_streaming_increment(chunk, tools)
+                        for chunk in chunks
+                    ]
+                    results.append(detector.finish(tools))
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        "".join(result.normal_text for result in results), ""
+                    )
+                    streamed = {}
+                    for result in results:
+                        for call in result.calls:
+                            entry = streamed.setdefault(
+                                call.tool_index, {"name": "", "arguments": ""}
+                            )
+                            entry["name"] += call.name or ""
+                            entry["arguments"] += call.parameters
+                    self.assertEqual(sorted(streamed), [0, 1])
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        [
+                            (streamed[i]["name"], json.loads(streamed[i]["arguments"]))
+                            for i in (0, 1)
+                        ],
+                        [("process", value) for value in arguments],
+                    )
+                    final = detector.finish(tools)
+                    self.assertEqual(final.calls, [])
+                    self.assertEqual(final.normal_text, "")
+
